title: Chelsea held squad meeting to support players after Wesley Fofana abuse – Liam Rosenior
content:
Chelsea had a meeting with the players on Friday as part of the club’s bid to help the group move on from Wesley Fofana being racially abused.

Fofana received racist messages on his Instagram account following the 1-1 draw at home to Burnley last weekend. The defender, who was sent off in the match, highlighted the posts he was sent and wrote: “2026, it’s still the same thing, nothing changes.”

Chelsea put out a statement of their own saying the club was “appalled and disgusted” and “the behaviour is completely unacceptable”.

Head coach Liam Rosenior revealed that Dr Michael Bennett, who was hired by the club last June as head of performance wellbeing from his role as director of player wellbeing at the Professional Footballers’ Association, met with the group on Friday morning.

When asked what help Chelsea have provided in light of the Fofana incident, Rosenior said: “The players have incredible support both on and off the pitch. They had a meeting with Doctor Michael Bennett today about his involvement in the club and how he can help with anything off the pitch.

“It was obviously a tough day for Wes, firstly what happened in the game and then the fall-out, the racist abuse he got online. Wes is a tough guy, a good guy.

“It is amazing, you (I) spoke about racism last week in the press conference and it affects you in ways that, it just shouldn’t exist whether it is online or verbal in person. It is something we have to do our best to eradicate from life let alone football. But Wes is absolutely fine, he has trained well this week.”

Fofana was one of four Premier League players racially abused last weekend. When asked if he has advised his squad to come off it for good in light of what has taken place, Rosenior added: “In terms of social media, the generation now, it is a part of the younger generation, part of their life.

“In a perfect world, players don’t take notice of what’s on social media but in reality they do because they are human beings. It is very easy to write whatever you want with no consequences when you are on social media.

“I hope that the players who are on it, who take those things in, take in the fact that it’s just noise, that it’s a lot of people with a lot of opinions. Some are valid and some come from a place where it is probably not a good place.”
